prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)

Purpose and stance
- Position the Lib Dems as the effective opposition to a likely Conservative majority.
- Oppose a hard Brexit; rule out coalition with Conservatives or Corbyn-led Labour.
- Seek a referendum on the final Brexit deal, with the option to remain.

Europe and Brexit
- Keep closest possible ties: single market, customs union, freedom of movement.
- Unilaterally guarantee EU citizens’ rights; secure UK citizens’ rights in EU.
- Protect Erasmus+, social/environmental protections, policing cooperation (Europol/EAW), research funding, and travel benefits.
- Defend devolved nations’ interests and Gibraltar.

NHS and social care
- Immediate 1p Income Tax rise ringfenced for NHS and social care; plan a dedicated health/care tax.
- Cross-party convention and independent budget watchdog for health/care.
- Integrate health and social care; cap care costs; support carers.
- Workforce: guarantee EU staff rights, end pay freeze, restore nurse bursaries, workforce plan.
- Mental health parity: waiting-time standards, crisis care, talking therapies.
- Public health: obesity strategy, sugar targets, smoking levy, PrEP on NHS, minimum unit pricing for alcohol.

Education and skills
- Nearly £7bn extra for schools/colleges; protect per-pupil funding; fair formula; protect Pupil Premium.
- Early years: triple Early Years Pupil Premium; raise quality.
- Oppose new grammars; restore local authority role in places/admissions; Ofsted reform.
- Curriculum: slimmed core incl PSHE/SRE, arts protected; better careers/vocational routes.
- Pupil wellbeing: school mental health support; free school meals for all primaries; breakfast clubs.
- Universities: reinstate maintenance grants; protect research and EU links; quality assurance.
- Lifelong learning: expand apprenticeships, adult skills accounts, credit transfer.

Economy and business
- Eliminate day-to-day deficit by 2020; borrow £100bn for infrastructure (300k homes/yr by 2022; hyperfast fibre; schools/hospitals; major rail; renewables).
- End 1% public sector pay cap; fair taxes (close loopholes, reverse some cuts, reform business rates; consider land value tax).
- Boost SMEs: expand British Business Bank, start-up allowance, rates reform.
- Innovation: protect/expand R&D; catapults; creative industries; nationwide FTTP; digital skills.
- Work and rights: genuine living wage review, modernise gig-economy rights, curb zero-hours abuse, stronger enforcement.
- Broader prosperity: employee ownership rights, worker voice on boards, regional devolution and investment, local banking.

Environment and energy
- Five green laws (transport, zero-carbon, nature, buildings, zero-waste).
- Air quality: diesel scrappage; ban new diesel cars/small vans by 2025; expand ULEZ; electrify buses/PHVs; EV infrastructure.
- Climate/energy: 80% cuts by 2040; net zero by 2050; 60% electricity from renewables by 2030; CCS; no fracking; conditional new nuclear; stay in Euratom.
- Homes: 4m insulation retrofits by 2022; zero-carbon homes restored; community energy; boost competition.
- Nature: £2bn flood fund; statutory natural capital targets; more green/blue protections; tree planting; animal welfare.
- Farming/fisheries: shift subsidies to public goods; fair supply chains; high import standards; TB vaccines; sustainable fisheries.
- Zero-waste: circular economy targets; 70% recycling; coffee cup levy; waste/incineration tax reform.

Families, housing, communities
- Childcare: expand free hours (from nine months for working parents as goal), extra paternity month, flexible work as day-one right.
- Welfare fairness: uprate benefits; scrap two-child cap/rape clause, bedroom tax; restore ESA; raise LHA; limit Winter Fuel Payment to higher-rate taxpayers.
- Housing: 300k homes/yr; 10 garden cities; lift council borrowing caps; British Housing & Infrastructure Bank; stronger planning/affordable housing; Rent to Own; Help to Rent; longer tenancies; end rough sleeping (Housing First).
- Transport: franchise reform incl public bids; electrification; HS2/HS3/Crossrail 2; Young Person’s Bus Card; bus regulation; cycling; regional links; oppose Heathrow/Gatwick expansion.
- Rural: universal superfast broadband; rural services/broadband funds; protect Post Office USO; rural affordable homes.
- Culture/sport: protect arts funding, BBC/Channel 4 independence; creative enterprise zones; safe standing.

Rights, justice, immigration
- Defend HRA/ECHR; digital bill of rights; tougher hate crime; independent media regulation.
- Policing: +£300m for community policing; end pay cap; body cameras; retain EU policing tools.
- Justice: presumption against short sentences; restorative/community justice; women’s/young justice boards; legal aid review.
- Drugs: decriminalise possession; legal, regulated cannabis; health-led policy.
- Counter-extremism: replace Prevent with community-led approach; end bulk data collection; protect encryption.
- Immigration: efficient, fair system; annual skills debate; remove students from net migration; restore post-study STEM visas; Migration Impact Fund; more ESOL.
- Refugees: safe/legal routes; 50,000 Syrians; 3,000 Dubs children; 28-day detention limit; faster claims; work rights after 6 months; protect LGBT+ asylum seekers.

International and defence
- Support UN/NATO/EU cooperation; 0.7% aid; stricter arms exports; suspend Saudi sales.
- Defence: spend 2% GDP; cyber investment; minimum nuclear deterrent with 3 boats, medium-readiness; support veterans.

Political reform and devolution
- STV for Commons and local; votes at 16; elected Lords; donation cap £10k; stronger lobbying/expenses rules; leaders’ debates.
- Constitutional convention for a federal UK; devolve repatriated powers.
- Oppose Scottish indyref2; more Welsh powers; support NI institutions and single market/customs union access.
- England: proportional English-only stage; devolution on demand; fair funding (retain Barnett, fix Wales underfunding).
